meta.evidenceNote: Retest counts are per test case mapped as failing the criterion. 'flagged' means a rule mapped to that test case reported an error, which can be a rule for a different criterion on the same page; 'asked for review' is axe incomplete or an HTML_CodeSniffer warning; 'notice' is an HTML_CodeSniffer notice; 'missed' means nothing relevant was reported.

automation.full: A rule can decide both pass and fail for the whole criterion.
automation.partial: Rules catch some failures or only flag items for review.

ai.likely: With the listed data, a capable model should judge it reliably.
ai.unlikely: Needs perception or judgement a model cannot verify well (real audio, lived assistive-technology experience, subjective adequacy).

human.must: Tools and AI cannot verify it well enough; a person must test.
human.should: AI can do a first pass; a person should confirm.

needs.dom: Rendered DOM with computed styles and scripts
needs.focus-trace: Sequence of focused elements with screenshots per Tab step
needs.zoomed-render: Renders at 200%/400% zoom or 320 CSS px width
needs.text-spacing-render: Render with the WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing override
needs.interaction: Scripted interaction (click, hover, type, key presses, viewport changes)
needs.multi-page: Several pages or steps of a process

review.pending: Borderline call; needs a human decision.

levels.primary: The pass where a tester verifies the criterion most efficiently in full; 'automated' is primary only when automation is 'full'.

automated.name: Automated rule checks
automated.summary: axe-core and HTML_CodeSniffer run over the page; the tools decide.

code-and-tree.name: Code and accessibility tree
code-and-tree.summary: Reading markup, the DOM and the accessibility tree for names, roles, states, relationships, language and structure.

visual.name: Visual inspection
visual.summary: Inspecting rendered screenshots for colour use, contrast, images of text, sensory instructions and consistent identification.

keyboard.name: Keyboard pass
keyboard.summary: Operating the page with the keyboard only: focus order, visible focus, traps, shortcuts, focus obscured and changes on focus or input.

screen-reader.name: Screen-reader pass
screen-reader.summary: Listening to, or reading, what a screen reader announces: reading order, status messages, link purpose in context.

zoom-reflow.name: Zoom and reflow
zoom-reflow.summary: Zoom to 200% and 400%, 320 CSS px reflow, text-spacing override, orientation, and content on hover or focus.

pointer-motion.name: Pointer and motion
pointer-motion.summary: Pointer gestures, cancellation, target size, dragging, motion actuation and label in name for speech input.

time-media.name: Time and media
time-media.summary: Time limits, moving and flashing content, autoplaying audio, captions, audio description, sign language and media alternatives.

language-cognition.name: Language and cognition
language-cognition.summary: Wording and content quality: descriptive headings and labels, unusual words, abbreviations, reading level, pronunciation, error suggestions and help.

multi-step-flow.name: Multi-step flow
multi-step-flow.summary: Processes over several steps or pages: error prevention, redundant entry, accessible authentication, consistency across pages, multiple ways and location.

automation.evidence: Retest (15 failing cases): axe 4 flagged, 11 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 1 asked for review, 5 notice, 5 missed. Rules detect missing or empty alternatives; whether the text is equivalent, or the image decorative, is only flagged as a notice.

ai.why: Comparing each image with its computed text alternative and surrounding text is a task vision models do well.

human.why: Equivalence for complex images (charts, diagrams) and context-dependent purpose needs confirmation.

1.1.1.rationale: The decision rests on the computed text alternative per image, read from markup and tree, checked against the picture.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 asked for review, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 notice. Rules only notice that audio or video exists and ask for a check; they cannot judge whether an alternative exists or is equivalent.

ai.why: A model can transcribe audio and describe video, then compare with the alternative, but equivalence errors are easy to miss.

human.why: Equivalence of the alternative to the media needs a person who has watched or listened to it.

1.2.1.rationale: Requires consuming the media and comparing it with its alternative.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. axe asks for review when a video has no track element; neither tool judges caption accuracy or synchronisation.

ai.why: Speech recognition can compare captions with the dialogue; non-speech sounds and timing are error-prone.

human.why: Caption accuracy, completeness and sync need a person to confirm.

1.2.2.rationale: Requires playing the media with captions on.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. The 1.2.3 sniff is only in the WCAG2AA ruleset; in WCAG2AAA the related 1.2.5/1.2.8 sniffs give page-level notices. axe has no rule.

ai.why: Deciding which visual information is important and whether the soundtrack or a text alternative conveys it needs reliable video understanding.

human.why: A person must watch the video and judge whether the important visual information is available.

1.2.3.rationale: Requires watching the video against its audio or text alternative.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. Only a notice asking for a manual check; live captions cannot be inspected from the page.

ai.why: Live events are hard to capture for analysis and captions depend on what happens live.

human.why: Needs a person observing a live stream.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only, emitted per video; no rule can tell whether an audio description track exists or is adequate.

ai.why: Judging whether description covers the important visual information needs reliable video understanding.

human.why: A person must watch with audio description and judge adequacy.

1.2.5.rationale: Requires watching the video with its audio description.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; no rule can detect sign-language interpretation.

ai.why: A model may notice that an interpreter is shown, but cannot verify the interpretation.

human.why: Only a sign-language user can judge the interpretation.

1.2.6.rationale: Media pass with a sign-language-competent tester.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; whether pauses are too short for standard description is a judgement.

ai.why: Requires judging whether standard description would be insufficient.

human.why: A person must watch and judge.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only, emitted per video; no rule checks for a full text alternative.

ai.why: A model can compare a transcript with transcribed audio and described video, but completeness is error-prone.

human.why: Completeness of the text alternative needs confirmation.

1.2.8.rationale: Requires consuming the media and reading its alternative.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; live audio cannot be inspected from the page.

ai.why: Live content cannot be captured reliably for analysis.

human.why: Needs a person observing the live audio.

automation.evidence: Retest (13 failing cases): axe 7 flagged, 6 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 5 flagged, 3 notice, 5 missed. Rules catch broken or missing markup patterns; structure that is visual only (bold text as headings, text lists, layout tables) is mostly a notice or missed.

ai.why: Comparing the visual structure in a screenshot with the semantics in the tree is a strength of current models.

human.why: Broad SC with many patterns; a person should confirm the AI's comparison.

1.3.1.rationale: Verified by comparing rendered structure with markup and the accessibility tree.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed. No rule compares DOM order with visual order or judges meaning.

ai.why: Comparing linearised reading order with the visual layout is tractable with both inputs.

human.why: Whether a different order changes meaning is a judgement to confirm.

1.3.2.rationale: Reading order is what a screen reader exposes; listening to the linear order is the most direct check.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed. Page-level notice only; no rule interprets instructions.

ai.why: Finding instructions that rely on shape, colour, size, location or sound is a reading task with a visual cross-check.

human.why: AI can do the first pass; borderline wording needs confirmation.

1.3.3.rationale: Instructions are read in the rendered page, where the referenced sensory cues are visible.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. axe detects CSS orientation locks in media queries; locks done in script or by the manifest are missed.

ai.why: Rendering in portrait and landscape viewports and comparing is straightforward.

human.why: Renders in both orientations settle it; the 'essential' exception is rare.

1.3.4.rationale: Checked by switching viewport orientation, alongside the other viewport tests.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 asked for review, 1 notice. axe validates autocomplete values that are present; neither tool can know which fields collect data about the user, so missing autocomplete is at best a notice.

ai.why: Matching field labels to the input-purpose list is a reliable reading task.

1.3.5.rationale: Pure markup check of autocomplete against field purpose.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Landmark rules (axe best-practice, not WCAG-tagged) catch missing regions; purpose of icons and components is not checked.

ai.why: Landmarks are easy; deciding which icons and components need programmatic purpose is open-ended.

1.3.6.rationale: Programmatic purpose lives in markup and the tree.

automation.evidence: Retest (4 failing cases): axe 4 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice, 3 missed. axe only checks links in text blocks; colour-only cues in forms, charts and states are missed.

ai.why: A greyscale render compared with the colour render shows information lost without colour.

human.why: Charts and state cues can be subtle; confirm.

1.4.1.rationale: Requires looking at the rendered page with and without colour.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. axe checks autoplaying media elements and asks for review when duration is unknown; HTML_CodeSniffer only gives a notice. Audio started by script is missed.

ai.why: Detecting audio playing for more than 3 seconds and a control near the top is observable in a scripted browser.

automation.evidence: Retest (7 failing cases): axe 6 flagged, 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 1 asked for review, 5 missed. axe decides plain text on solid backgrounds well but returns 'needs review' over images, gradients and overlaps. HTML_CodeSniffer at WCAG2AAA uses the 1.4.6 sniff, so many 1.4.3 failures surface only as 1.4.6 codes.

ai.why: Pixel sampling of rendered text plus computed styles covers the cases rules cannot compute.

human.why: Tools plus pixel-based AI checks suffice.

1.4.3.rationale: Rules handle most cases; the remainder is judged on the rendered screenshot.

automation.evidence: Retest (4 failing cases): axe 4 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 missed. axe only catches viewport settings that block zoom; text clipped or overlapping at 200% is not tested. The 1.4.4 sniff is not in the WCAG2AAA ruleset.

ai.why: Comparing 100% and 200% renders for clipped, overlapping or missing text is feasible.

human.why: Overlap and truncation in screenshots are easy to overlook; confirm.

automation.evidence: Retest (5 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 3 notice. Only notices for every image; the retest 'flagged' results come from missing-alt rules on the same images, not from an images-of-text check.

ai.why: Recognising text inside images is reliable; the 'essential' and customisable exceptions need judgement.

human.why: AI covers it; edge cases are logos and essential presentations.

1.4.5.rationale: Images of text are found by looking at rendered images.

automation.evidence: Retest (9 failing cases): axe 8 flagged, 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 1 asked for review, 7 missed. Same limits as 1.4.3: text over images, gradients and overlaps cannot be computed. axe flags most cases via color-contrast or color-contrast-enhanced.

ai.why: Pixel sampling covers what rules cannot compute.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; background level in mixed audio cannot be measured by page rules.

ai.why: Separating speech from background in a mixed track and judging 20 dB is not reliable.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notices only, one per requirement; no rule decides line length, justification, spacing or colour selection.

ai.why: Line length, justification and spacing are measurable from computed styles; user colour selection and 200% without horizontal scroll need interaction.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only, emitted once per page with images.

ai.why: Recognising text in images is reliable.

1.4.9.rationale: Found by looking at rendered images.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. HTML_CodeSniffer warns about fixed-width elements that may scroll in two dimensions; axe has no rule.

ai.why: Rendering at 320 CSS px, checking scroll width and comparing content is scriptable.

human.why: Loss of content or function at 320 px and the 2D-layout exception need confirmation.

automation.evidence: Retest (4 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 1 notice, 2 missed. No WCAG-tagged axe rule; HTML_CodeSniffer's 1.4.11 sniff is a notice. Retest detections came from text-contrast and focus rules on the same pages.

ai.why: Identifying which graphics and component boundaries are required, in every state, is error-prone; the pixel maths is easy.

human.why: Deciding what is required for understanding needs confirmation.

1.4.11.rationale: Visual inspection of components, states and graphics.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. axe only finds inline !important spacing that blocks overrides; clipping after the override is not tested.

ai.why: Comparing renders before and after the text-spacing bookmarklet styles shows clipping and overlap.

human.why: Confirm clipping found or missed in screenshots.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notice only; dismissable, hoverable and persistent behaviour needs interaction.

ai.why: A scripted agent can hover, focus, press Escape and move into the popup, but finding all triggers is error-prone.

1.4.13.rationale: Checked during the magnified-view pass, where hover content matters most.

automation.evidence: Retest (5 failing cases): axe 5 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 5 missed. Rules catch a few patterns; operability of custom controls with the keyboard needs interaction.

ai.why: An agent can tab through and operate controls, but finding every pointer-only function is error-prone.

human.why: A keyboard pass by a person is quick and reliable.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only; traps appear only when focus moves.

ai.why: A focus trace that stops cycling through the page shows a trap.

human.why: Confirm escape methods advised to the user.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Same limits as 2.1.1, without exceptions.

ai.why: Same as 2.1.1.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; shortcuts live in script.

ai.why: Pressing printable keys outside inputs and watching for actions can find shortcuts; script reading helps.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch meta refresh only; script timers and session timeouts are missed. The 2.2.1 sniff is missing from the WCAG2AAA ruleset; the WCAG2AA supplement (D-024) catches the meta refresh cases.

ai.why: Waiting and observing can reveal limits; long or server-side limits are hard to trigger.

human.why: Confirm the limit and the adjust/extend options.

automation.evidence: Retest (4 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 missed. Rules catch obsolete blink and marquee only; CSS/JS animation and auto-updating content are missed.

ai.why: Screenshots over time show motion; finding and testing pause controls is error-prone.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Same limits as 2.2.1, without exceptions.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch meta refresh only; script interruptions such as pop-ups and live updates are missed.

ai.why: Observing a page over time reveals interruptions; whether they can be postponed needs interaction.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only; session expiry is server behaviour.

ai.why: Requires letting a session expire mid-process and checking data survives; slow and environment-dependent.

human.why: Session behaviour on a real system needs confirmation.

2.2.5.rationale: Tested along a multi-step process with a session expiry.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; data-loss timeouts are server behaviour.

ai.why: Can read warnings in the flow; verifying actual timeout duration is slow.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Neither tool analyses flashing. Dedicated flash analysers (outside our toolset) can decide this from video frames.

ai.why: Only with frame-accurate capture fed to a flash analyser; models cannot judge flashes from sparse screenshots.

human.why: Use a flash analyser rather than human viewing, which is risky; a person confirms the result.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notice only; see 2.3.1.

ai.why: Same as 2.3.1; the count rule (no more than three) is simpler than the threshold.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Comparing behaviour with and without prefers-reduced-motion emulation finds some cases.

human.why: Whether motion is essential is a judgement.

automation.evidence: No test case in the 2026 retest. axe checks for a skip link, heading or landmark; HTML_CodeSniffer checks skip-link targets and frame titles. Whether the mechanism works is not tested.

ai.why: Landmarks, headings and a working skip link are visible in tree and focus trace.

2.4.1.rationale: Markup and tree check, confirmed in the keyboard pass.

automation.evidence: Retest (7 failing cases): axe 5 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 3 missed. Rules catch missing or empty titles; whether the title describes topic or purpose is only a notice.

ai.why: Judging a title against page content is an easy reading task.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice, 1 missed. HTML_CodeSniffer only notices tabindex use; axe's tabindex rule is best-practice. Order without tabindex (CSS reordering, dialogs) is missed.

ai.why: Overlaying the focus sequence on the screenshot shows illogical jumps.

human.why: Whether order preserves meaning is a judgement to confirm.

automation.evidence: Retest (5 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 2 asked for review, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 3 notice. Rules catch links with no name; vague names are at best a notice. The 2.4.4 sniff is only in the WCAG2AA ruleset.

ai.why: Judging link names with their programmatic context is a reliable reading task.

2.4.4.rationale: Link purpose as announced with its context; also answerable from the tree.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only; needs knowledge of the whole site.

ai.why: Looking for search, sitemap, navigation or links across pages is straightforward.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Judging whether headings and labels describe content is a reading task.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice, 1 missed. Page-level notice only, not tied to the element; axe has no rule.

ai.why: Diffing screenshots before and after each focus move shows whether an indicator appears.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notices only.

ai.why: Breadcrumbs, current-page indicators and step indicators are recognisable.

automation.evidence: Retest (9 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 2 asked for review, 5 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 7 notice. Rules catch empty links; vague link text is a notice per link.

ai.why: Judging link names alone is a reading task.

2.4.9.rationale: Accessible names of links, read without context.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule decides whether content should be organised with headings.

ai.why: Spotting sections without headings is a structure-reading task.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule.

ai.why: Bounding boxes of the focused element versus sticky or overlay elements can be computed per focus step.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. No rule.

ai.why: Same as 2.4.11 with full visibility required.

automation.evidence: Retest (4 failing cases): axe 4 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 notice, 1 missed. Only the page-level 2.4.7 notice; no rule measures indicator area or change contrast.

ai.why: Area and 3:1 change contrast can be computed from focused/unfocused screenshot pairs, but the measurement rules are fiddly.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; gestures live in script.

ai.why: Script reading can find multipoint or path handlers and look for single-pointer alternatives.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule.

ai.why: Down-event handlers can be found in script and tested with press-and-move-away.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 1 notice. axe's rule is experimental and covers some widgets; the retest detections came from missing-label rules on the same pages, not from a mismatch check.

ai.why: Comparing visible label text with the accessible name is reliable.

human.why: AI suffices; speech-input testing confirms if wanted.

2.5.3.rationale: Most efficiently verified by comparing tree names with visible labels, although the barrier affects speech-input users.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule.

ai.why: devicemotion/deviceorientation listeners are findable in script; real-device behaviour is not.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. axe's target-size checks the 24 px minimum (2.5.8), so it only catches 2.5.5 failures that are also below 24 px.

ai.why: Target bounding boxes are computable; exceptions (inline, equivalent) need judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule.

ai.why: Script reading can find pointer-type restrictions.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule.

ai.why: Drag interactions and alternatives can be found; operating them reliably is harder.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. axe measures size and spacing; exceptions (inline, equivalent control, essential) and overlapping targets can need review.

ai.why: Target geometry is computable.

automation.evidence: Retest (8 failing cases): axe 6 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 4 missed. Rules catch missing or invalid lang; a valid code for the wrong language passes.

ai.why: Identifying the language of the text and comparing with lang is reliable.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed. Rules catch invalid lang values on elements; passages in another language without lang are missed.

ai.why: Language identification of passages is reliable; proper names and loanwords are exceptions.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Finding jargon and idioms is feasible; what is 'unusual' depends on audience.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Finding abbreviations and checking for an expansion is a reading task.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Estimating reading level and spotting a simpler version is a strength of language models.

human.why: Readability formulas are language-specific; the level is a judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

ai.why: Finding words whose meaning depends on pronunciation is language-specific and rare.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice, 1 missed. Notice for every input, not tied to behaviour.

ai.why: Watching URL, window, focus and DOM changes on each focus move detects context changes.

human.why: Change of context versus change of content is a judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 2 missed. HTML_CodeSniffer flags forms without a submit button; auto-submitting scripts are missed.

ai.why: Changing each control and watching for context changes is scriptable.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only; needs several pages.

ai.why: Comparing navigation order across pages is a diff.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only; needs several pages.

ai.why: Comparing icons and names of same-function components across pages is feasible.

3.2.4.rationale: Visual and name comparison across pages.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 2 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 3 flagged. Rules catch meta refresh and notice new-window links; script redirects and pop-ups are missed.

ai.why: target attributes, redirects and pop-ups are detectable.

3.2.5.rationale: Mostly markup and script inspection with a little interaction.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; needs several pages.

ai.why: Comparing location and order of help mechanisms across pages is a diff.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 2 notice. Notice once per form; errors only exist after submission. The retest 'flagged' result came from a contrast rule on the same page.

ai.why: Submitting invalid data and reading errors and their associations is scriptable.

human.why: Confirm the error is perceivable in text and programmatically.

3.3.1.rationale: Requires going through a form with invalid input.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch missing labels; whether labels and instructions suffice is a notice.

ai.why: Reading labels and required-format hints is reliable.

3.3.2.rationale: Markup and tree check of form fields.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice once per form.

ai.why: Triggering errors and judging whether suggestions are given is feasible.

human.why: Quality of suggestions is a judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only; the 3.3.4 sniff is only in the WCAG2AA ruleset (the retest notice came from the 3.3.6 AllForms code).

ai.why: Needs to decide whether the transaction is legal/financial and to complete it to test review, check or reversal.

human.why: Real transactions are risky to test automatically.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice once per form.

ai.why: Help presence is easy to find; whether it is context-sensitive and adequate is a judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 notice. Notice once per form.

ai.why: Same as 3.3.4 for all submissions.

automation.evidence: Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; needs a multi-step process.

ai.why: Walking a process and comparing requested data across steps is feasible.

human.why: Essential and security exceptions need judgement.

automation.evidence: Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. No rule detects a cognitive function test; paste blocking lives in script.

ai.why: Can spot CAPTCHAs and test paste and autofill; recognising every cognitive test and acceptable alternatives is error-prone.

automation.evidence: Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed. No rule.
